event:
I withdrew the finding. The HMAC DV environment does check the `fifo_empty` interrupt, so the requirement is not planned-only.

The scoreboard (`hw/ip/hmac/dv/env/hmac_scoreboard.sv:693`) predicts the interrupt as raised when the FIFO runs empty after having been full. That prediction feeds `intr_state` (line 391), which is compared on CSR reads, so a wrong interrupt fails the test. The smoke sequence (`hmac_smoke_vseq.sv`) supplies the stimulus and reads the state. Only a short timing-corner-case window is excluded from the check.

The software tests don't settle it either way. `hmac_enc_test.c` enables the interrupt but never asserts that it fires.

I did not run the DV regression, so this rests on reading the scoreboard and sequence code.
